shots.say: Oh no! Our little tree is droopy. It is so thirsty!
Hello, I'm Milo! This is our zoo garden, with Sandy the baby camel, and Tumble the baby elephant.
I'll water it! Oh. The watering can is empty.
Our tree needs water every day, and we have none left.
The oasis has lots of water. Let's walk there, and bring some back for the tree!
Mama camel puts two little jugs on Sandy's back. Stay together, and be home by supper.
Is the little tree happy, or thirsty?
Bye, Mama camel! We'll be back by supper!
Off they go, over the dunes. The oasis is far, far away.
How many jugs does Sandy carry? Count with me! One. Two!
Flap, flap, flap. Phew! My wings are tired.
Rest on my back, Milo! I can carry a little bird.
Milo lands softly on Sandy's back. Ahh, that's better!
Who is carrying Milo now? Sandy, or Tumble?
On the rocky trail, the sun is hot, hot, hot.
Phew! I'm so hot. My big ears go flap, flap, like fans!
Let's rest in the shade of the big rock.
They sit down in the cool shade. Tumble flaps his ears, and soon he feels better.
Can you flap your ears like Tumble? Flap, flap, flap!
Where is it cool? In the sun, or in the shade?
At last, the oasis! Cool blue water, and tall palm trees.
Tumble drinks with his trunk. Slurp! And Sandy drinks, and drinks, and drinks.
Milo has a tiny sip. A little bird needs only a little drink.
A very thirsty camel can drink thirty gallons of water, in only thirteen minutes!
shots.tag: fact: thirty gallons in thirteen minutes

shots.say: Which is more water? One jug, or thirty jugs?
Glug, glug! Milo helps fill the two little jugs, all the way to the top.
On the way back, the sand is soft and deep. And the jugs are heavy now.
I'll carry a jug with my trunk! Oh, oh! It wobbles. Splish!
I'll carry one! Ooh, it's too heavy for a little bird.
Is a full jug heavy, or light?
They sit down on the sandy hill. The sun is low, and the zoo is still far away.
Tumble is hot, my wings are tired, and the jugs are so heavy.
Maybe our little tree can't have a drink today.
Don't worry, friends. We are together. Let me think.
Who can carry the heavy jugs? Milo, or Sandy?
I know! Camels are made for carrying, and for walking far. I can carry the jugs, step by step!
Grown-up camels can carry big, heavy loads, and walk a long way every day.
Milo hops on top. Tumble walks beside her. Step, step, step, slow and steady.
Sandy, aren't you thirsty?
Not yet! I had a big drink at the oasis.
A camel can go a week or more without water!
Wow! A whole week!
Can a camel go a week without water? Yes, or no?
shots.tag: question: a week yes or no

shots.say: Can you walk slow and steady, like Sandy? Step, step, step!
Step by step, slow and steady. Here comes water! Tree, get ready!
Back at the zoo, the little tree is waiting.
Tumble pours the water. Glug, glug, glug! The little tree drinks.
Look! Its leaves stand up, green and happy!
How does the little tree look now? Droopy, or happy?
Mama camel nuzzles Sandy. She is so proud of her.
Thank you, Sandy. You carried the water all the way!
And we all helped, together!
Thank you for walking with me, Tumble and Milo!
Little steps can go a long, long way, when friends help each other.
Do you remember? How long can a camel go without water? A week, or a year?
Who carried the jugs home? Sandy, or Milo?
Step by step, slow and steady. Here comes water! Tree, get ready!
Next time: Sandy's first night away! See you on the next adventure, friends!
